sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever felt stuck in a loop you couldn't escape? Today we'll learn how to control loops like a pro!

• How to exit loops early with `break`
• How to skip to the next iteration with `continue`
• When to use each keyword effectively

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're searching for your favorite book in a library:

- `break` is like finding the book and immediately leaving the library
- `continue` is like skipping a shelf that doesn't have your book and moving to the next one

**The `break` keyword**
• Immediately exits the current loop
• Program continues with the next statement after the loop
• Works with `for`, `while`, and `do-while` loops

**The `continue` keyword**
• Skips the current iteration and jumps to the next one
• The loop condition is re-evaluated
• Only skips the current cycle, doesn't exit the loop

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Both work with all loop types (for, while, do-while)
✓ Use `break` when you've found what you're looking for
✓ Use `continue` when you want to skip specific cases

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use `break` to exit loops early when the job is done
Use `continue` to skip invalid or unwanted data
Add comments explaining why you're using these keywords
donts: Don't use `break` just to exit a loop - make your conditions clear
Don't nest too many `break`/`continue` statements - it gets confusing
Don't forget that `break` only exits the innermost loop
sections.protip: For nested loops, label your loops and use `break labelName;` to exit outer loops!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where are these keywords used in real apps?

examples.how: Use `break` when you find the item you're searching for in a list
Use `continue` to skip invalid or corrupted data entries
Use `break` to exit game loops when the player quits

problem.description:
Write a program that prints numbers from 1 to 10, but:
- Skips printing 5 using `continue`
- Stops printing after 8 using `break`
hints: Use an if statement to check when i equals 5
Use another if statement to check when i equals 8
problem.explanation: The program prints numbers 1-4, skips 5, prints 6-8, then exits before reaching 9. The output will be: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 `break` exits loops completely - use when you're done
📌 `continue` skips to the next iteration - use to filter data
📌 Practice using both in simple loops first
📌 Ready to learn about nested loops next!
